@Ploppy3  **This is not a bug.**
Here is a updated link. which works as you expected.
 [stackblitz](https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-bqbf8m)
The reason why the div is not animated is when your page is in a enter state, the div element is already entered in its parent earlier ! so the '@redToBlack' bind to the div won't work as expected,because the div is not match the ':enter' state.

The right way to do is bind the 'redToBack' to the **_ page_**:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12789732/57904826-f4e40800-78a6-11e9-96c1-528688d167eb.png)
and modify the animation definition using query to find the div ,then animate it ！
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12789732/57904863-19d87b00-78a7-11e9-8067-11b737ba6d80.png)

@GISerWYJ Sorry but this is not what I want, I want the individual elements/components of my page to render with their own animation. This is a minimal reproduction of the problem. I don't want the page to be animated. 

Nb: If you look closely your animation has a issue where the previous page disappear instantly.

I'm having the exact same problem.  I've tried just about every possible way I can think of to get animations to run on the pages that are entering/leaving and it just ignores them.  

Edit 1:

It appears to ignore all child animations completely if the animation is on an element of the page being transitioned.  However if I apply an animation to the page component via host binding, then use animateChild in THAT trigger (essentially going 2 levels deep with animateChild), it does something.  Unfortunately, what it does is completely remove the leaving page instantly with no animations at all.  But hey, at least something changed...

Can we get a status update? Is someone working on this? Are there any suggested workarounds? 

Basic functionality being broken, without comment, for 6-7 major releases is not a great position to be in.

For clarity, Angular 7 was released in October of 2018. A feature that's listed in the official docs at least four times has been broken for three (3!) years without comment or movement. 

What's going on?

I'm unable to implement my team's visual+motion design using Angular animations because basic, documented, functionality is broken. It's been two years since this featured was accepted as broken, is there any kind of an update?
@jelbourn Would you consider bumping this to `P2` as it's such a fundamental bit of functionality.
